summary: Hyon Gak Sunim works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1987–1988), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under the traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan (2009–2016). He held posts at Kyushu University (2017–2019) and Chonnam National University (2019).

Hywel David Lewis was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bangor University (~1929–1933) and Jesus College, Oxford (~1933–1936), and later held a post at Bangor University (~1936–1955).

Hélène Brunner-Lachaux was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jean Filliozat at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1958–1962). She held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1960–2000) and the CNRS (1963–1985).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and served as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from the University of Cambridge and Lancaster University. He served as Reader at St Martin's College (~1985–2007) and Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Cumbria (~2007–2014).

Ian James Coghlan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and served as a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute at Monash University (attested 2005).

Ian Kesarcodi-Watson worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Melbourne, Oxford, McMaster (under John G. Arapura), and Pune, later serving as Lecturer at the University of Hong Kong (1971–1975) and Senior Lecturer at La Trobe University (1975–1984).
Ian Kishizawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Oxford (~1959–1963), he held posts at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Aichi Bunkyo University (2000).

Ian Reader works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, having completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983). He held academic posts at Stirling (~1989–1999), Lancaster (~1999–2006), and Manchester (~2006–2015).

Ibrahim Shah is a scholar of archaeology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Peshawar (2001–2007). He held posts at the University of Peshawar starting in 2001 and at Hazara University as Associate Professor and Department Chairman.

Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959), where he later held an academic post (~1970–2007), and taught at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978).

Ichiro Hori was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1963) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kogen Mizuno at Komazawa University (~1965–1967) and attended Otani University (~1967–1970). He held faculty posts at Komazawa University from 1975 and as professor (1985–2013).

Ichiro Numata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held part-time lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ichisada Miyazaki was a Sinology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) under Jitsuzo Kuwabara (~1922–1931). He subsequently held an academic post at Kyoto University (~1936–1965).
Ida Vassalini was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She completed degrees at the University of Padua (~1910–1914) and the University of Milan, where she also held a teaching post.

Ignatij Andreevich Kossovich was a linguistics scholar who studied at Vilnius University (~1826–1830) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1831–1833). He served as Professor of Greek at Polotsk Uniate Theological Seminary (1833–1835) and the University of Warsaw (1872–1878).
Ignazio Guidi studied at Sapienza University of Rome. He later served as a professor at Sapienza University of Rome from 1876 to 1919.
